eosinophilic esophagitis—abnormal inﬁ ltration of eosinophils 
into the esophagus; may be associated with food allergy as well 
as other conditions such as scleroderma, gastroesophageal 
reﬂ ux disease, and infection
epidemiology—the study of the rates of disease within a given 
population
epidural—refers to placement of a drug into the spinal ﬂ uid
epidural anesthesia—an anesthetic drug placed into the epi-
dural space of the lumbar or sacral region of the spine, causing 
loss of sensation from the abdomen and pelvis to the lower 
limbs
epigastric—referring to the upper abdominal region
epigenetics—inheritance of information based on gene expres-
sion levels rather than gene sequence; regulated by genomic
modiﬁ cations such as DNA methylation and histone methyla-
tion or acetylation
epilepsy—a neurological disorder characterized by recurrent 
seizures, generally more than two unprovoked seizures
epinephrine—a chemical made by the adrenal gland that
relaxes smooth muscles, constricts blood vessels, regulates 
arterial blood pressure, and prepares body for “ﬁ ght or ﬂ ight”
responses; when it is used to treat severe allergic reactions, it is
sometimes referred to as adrenaline (an older term)
